methods.name: run_skill
methods.doc: Execute a Python skill using this connection and its existing loop.

methods.name: robot
methods.doc:
The backend this client drives, built on first read when a bare
client (what a user script constructs) supplied none.

methods.name: tool
methods.doc: Active bound tool. Raises if no tool has been set.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
Release UDP transport and background tasks.

Safe to call multiple times.

methods.name: home
methods.doc:
Home the robot to its home position.

Uncalibrated (first home after power-on), this runs the full
referencing sequence: each joint seeks its limit switch, then the
robot moves to standby. Calibrated, it returns to standby with a
normal planned, collision-checked joint move — unless
``calibrate=True``, which re-runs the referencing sequence. The
referencing sequence is firmware-driven and ignores the collision
world, so clear keep-out geometry from the joints' sweep first.

Returns the command index (≥ 0) on success, -1 on failure.

Category: Motion

Example:
    rbt.home()

Args:
    wait: If True, block until motion completes
    calibrate: If True, always run the referencing sequence
    timeout: Maximum time to wait in seconds (only used when wait=True)

methods.name: teleport
methods.doc:
Instantly set joint angles and optional tool positions (simulator only).

The pose is exact, so the arm counts as homed afterwards and
planned motion may follow. Whatever was driving the arm is
cancelled with ``MOTN_CANCELLED``.

Category: Control

Example:
    rbt.teleport([90, -90, 180, 0, 0, 180])
    rbt.teleport([90, -90, 180, 0, 0, 180], tool_positions=[1.0])

Returns:
    1 once the pose is applied, 0 when no reply arrives.

Raises:
    ValueError: for a non-finite angle, one outside the hard joint
        limits, or a tool position outside ``[0, 1]``.
    MotionError: off the simulator (``SYS_NOT_SIMULATOR``), when the
        tool positions do not match the fitted tool's DOF count, or
        while the controller is disabled.

methods.name: stop
methods.doc:
Stop all motion — cancel the active move and clear the queue.

The controller stays enabled and holding position; the next motion
command is accepted immediately.

Category: Control

Example:
    rbt.stop()

Returns:
    1 if acknowledged, 0 on failure.

methods.name: estop
methods.doc:
Protective stop: stop all motion and latch the controller
disabled until ``reset()``.

Category: Control

Example:
    rbt.estop()

Returns:
    1 if acknowledged, 0 on failure.

methods.name: reset
methods.doc:
Clear a latched protective stop, re-enabling motion.

Category: Control

Example:
    rbt.reset()

Returns:
    1 if acknowledged, 0 on failure.

methods.name: simulator
methods.doc:
Enable or disable simulator mode.

Category: Control

Example:
    rbt.simulator(True)

methods.name: is_simulator
methods.doc:
Query whether simulator mode is active.

Category: Query

Example:
    active = rbt.is_simulator()

methods.name: connect_hardware
methods.doc:
Connect to robot hardware via serial port.

Category: Configuration

Example:
    rbt.connect_hardware("/dev/ttyUSB0")

Args:
    port_str: Serial port path (e.g., '/dev/ttyUSB0' or 'COM3').

Returns:
    1 if acknowledged, 0 on failure.

Raises:
    ValueError: If port_str is empty.

methods.name: reset_state
methods.doc:
Reset program state — world shapes, tool selection, errors, pause,
motion profile and execution speed — and discard the queue, each
discarded command failing with ``MOTN_CANCELLED``.

The arm holds where it is. A protective stop stays latched (only
``reset()`` clears it), and homed state, digital outputs and the
serial connection are kept.

Category: Control

Example:
    rbt.reset_state()

methods.name: ping
methods.doc:
Return parsed ping result with hardware_connected status.

Category: Query

Example:
    rbt.ping()

methods.name: angles
methods.doc:
Current joint angles in degrees [J1, J2, J3, J4, J5, J6].

Category: Query

Example:
    angles = rbt.angles()

methods.name: io
methods.doc:
Digital I/O status [in1, in2, out1, out2, estop].

``timeout`` bounds setup, retries, and the reply; None uses client defaults.

Category: Query

Example:
    io = rbt.io()

methods.name: joint_speeds
methods.doc:
Current joint velocities in deg/s [J1, J2, J3, J4, J5, J6], the
units of ``StatusBuffer.speeds``.

Category: Query

Example:
    speeds = rbt.joint_speeds()

methods.name: pose
methods.doc:
Current TCP pose as [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz] in mm and degrees.

Category: Query

Example:
    pose = rbt.pose()

methods.name: status
methods.doc:
Aggregate status snapshot (pose, angles, speeds, io, tool_status).
Its ``tool_status`` is always a ``ToolStatus``, key ``"NONE"`` when
no tool is fitted.

Category: Query

Example:
    status = rbt.status()

methods.name: loop_stats
methods.doc:
Fetch control-loop runtime metrics.

Category: Query

Example:
    stats = rbt.loop_stats()

methods.name: reset_loop_stats
methods.doc:
Reset control-loop min/max metrics and overrun count.

Category: Query

Example:
    rbt.reset_loop_stats()

methods.name: execution_speed
methods.doc:
Read fresh requested, applied, and retained execution scales.

Category: Query

Example:
    speed = rbt.execution_speed()

methods.name: set_execution_speed
methods.doc:
Select 10–100% of planned queued-motion speed, preserving pause.

Category: Control

Example:
    rbt.set_execution_speed(0.5)

methods.name: pause
methods.doc:
Request a controlled hold, retaining queued trajectory progress.

A confirmed request returns 1. Read ``execution_speed().paused``
to confirm the hold. Standalone Python completion timeouts continue.

Category: Control

Example:
    rbt.pause()

methods.name: resume
methods.doc:
Resume the retained queue at its selected positive speed.

Category: Control

Example:
    rbt.resume()

methods.name: set_status_rate
methods.doc:
Set the rate the controller broadcasts status at.

Category: Configuration

Example:
    rbt.set_status_rate(100)

methods.name: status_rate
methods.doc:
Current broadcast rate and the control rate it divides.

Category: Query

Example:
    rate = rbt.status_rate()

methods.name: tools
methods.doc:
Current tool and available tools.

Category: Query

Example:
    tools = rbt.tools()

methods.name: select_tool
methods.doc:
Set the active end-effector tool on the controller.

Category: Configuration

Example:
    rbt.select_tool("PNEUMATIC")

Args:
    tool_name: Name of the tool ('NONE', 'PNEUMATIC', 'SSG-48', 'MSG', 'VACUUM')
    variant_key: Optional variant within the tool type.

Returns:
    Command index (>= 0) if queued, 0 on failure.

methods.name: set_tcp_offset
methods.doc:
Set TCP offset in mm, composed on top of the current tool transform.

The offset shifts the effective TCP point in the tool's local frame.
Subsequent motion (especially TRF relative moves) will use the new TCP.
Returns the queued index; await ``wait_command(index)`` to confirm
application. This translation-only setter clears user TCP rotation.
Call with (0, 0, 0) to reset. Changing tools resets the offset.

Category: Configuration

Example:
    rbt.set_tcp_offset(0, 0, -190)  # pencil tip 190mm from gripper

methods.name: set_shapes
methods.doc:
Replace the program-layer collision-world shapes (keep-out barriers).

Collision-enabled shapes are added to the controller's checkers so motion
is blocked against them; an empty list clears the program layer.
Installation-layer shapes (robot config) are unaffected.

Acknowledged: returns 1 only after the controller confirms the world
was applied; 0 on timeout. Raises MotionError if the controller
rejects the shapes.

Category: Configuration

Example:
    rbt.set_shapes([Box(name="table", x=0.6, y=0.4, z=0.02,
                        pose=(0.3, 0, -0.01, 0, 0, 0))])

methods.name: shapes
methods.doc:
The collision world the controller is currently enforcing, by layer.

Readback truth for displays; re-query when ``StatusBuffer.scene_epoch``
changes. Returns None if the controller is unreachable.

Category: Query

Example:
    world = rbt.shapes()

methods.name: tcp_offset
methods.doc:
Query current TCP offset in mm [x, y, z].

Category: Configuration

Example:
    offset = rbt.tcp_offset()

methods.name: select_profile
methods.doc:
Set the motion profile (e.g. ``"TOPPRA"``).

Category: Configuration

Example:
    rbt.select_profile("TOPPRA")

Args:
    profile: Motion profile type ('TOPPRA', 'RUCKIG', 'QUINTIC', 'TRAPEZOID', 'LINEAR')
        Note: RUCKIG is point-to-point only; Cartesian moves will use TOPPRA.

Returns:
    1 once the profile is selected, 0 when no reply arrives.

Raises:
    MotionError: when ``profile`` is not a profile name.

methods.name: profile
methods.doc:
Current motion profile name.

Category: Query

Example:
    profile = rbt.profile()

methods.name: activity
methods.doc:
What the robot is currently doing.

Returns state (idle/executing/error), current command name,
parameters, and error description if applicable.

Category: Query

Example:
    act = rbt.activity()

methods.name: queue
methods.doc:
Queued command list.

Category: Query

Example:
    queue = rbt.queue()

methods.name: reachable
methods.doc:
Remaining freedom of movement per joint/axis before hitting limits.

Category: Query

Example:
    en = rbt.reachable()

methods.name: error
methods.doc:
Current error state, or None if no error.

Category: Query

Example:
    err = rbt.error()

methods.name: tcp_speed
methods.doc:
TCP linear velocity in mm/s.

Category: Query

Example:
    speed = rbt.tcp_speed()

methods.name: is_estop_pressed
methods.doc:
Check if E-stop is pressed. Returns True if pressed.

Category: Query

Example:
    pressed = rbt.is_estop_pressed()

methods.name: is_robot_stopped
methods.doc:
Check if robot has stopped moving.

Category: Query

Prefer ``wait_command()`` for waiting on specific commands.
This method polls raw joint speeds and is mainly useful for
diagnostics or manual stopping logic.

Example:
    stopped = rbt.is_robot_stopped()

Args:
    threshold_speed: Speed threshold in deg/s

Returns:
    True if all joints below threshold

methods.name: wait_motion
methods.doc:
Wait until the queue has run out and the arm has come to rest.

First waits for the latest command the controller has accepted —
every command this client queued, and each newer one the status
stream reports accepted — to end, then for the arm to hold still
for ``settle_window``. A command that failed or was cancelled ends
the wait like one that completed; ``wait_command()`` tells which.

Category: Synchronization

Example:
    rbt.wait_motion()

Args:
    timeout: Maximum time to wait in seconds
    settle_window: How long robot must be stable to be considered stopped
    speed_threshold: Max joint speed to be considered stopped (deg/s)
    angle_threshold: Max angle change to be considered stopped (degrees)

Returns:
    True if robot stopped, False if timeout

Raises:
    ConnectionError: If the controller session changes while a
        command is still being waited on.

methods.name: wait_ready
methods.doc:
Poll ping() until server responds or timeout.

Args:
    timeout: Maximum time to wait for server to respond
    interval: Polling interval between ping attempts

Returns:
    True if server responded to PING, False on timeout

methods.name: wait_status
methods.doc: Wait until a multicast status satisfies predicate(status) within timeout.

methods.name: wait_command
methods.doc:
Wait until a specific command index has been completed.

Queries exact success in the controller's last 1024 completions: a
later command that finishes first — a jog, a ``tool.stop()`` — does
not complete an unfinished one queued before it. Queued commands,
tool actions among them, run in index order, so a wait on one covers
everything queued ahead of it.
Unknown or expired results are never inferred successful from the
status high-water mark. A command that ended as a failure — cancelled
by ``stop()``/``estop()`` (``MOTN_CANCELLED``) or failed by the
pipeline — raises MotionError.

Args:
    command_index: The command index to wait for (returned by motion commands).
    timeout: Maximum time to wait in seconds.

Returns:
    True if the command completed within timeout, False otherwise.

Raises:
    MotionError: If the pipeline errored at or before command_index.

methods.name: move_j
methods.doc:
Joint-space move. Positional arg = joint angles; pose= kwarg = Cartesian target with IK.

Returns the command index (≥ 0) on success, -1 on failure.

Category: Motion

Example:
    rbt.move_j([90, -90, 180, 0, 0, 180], speed=0.5)

Args:
    angles: 6 joint angles in degrees (ignored if pose= is set)
    pose: If set, Cartesian target [x,y,z,rx,ry,rz] — dispatches to MOVEJ_POSE
    duration: Motion duration in seconds; > 0 times the move and speed is unused
    speed: Speed fraction in (0, 1], used when duration is 0
    accel: Acceleration fraction in (0, 1]
    r: Blend radius in mm (0 = stop at target)
    rel: If True, angles are relative to current position
    wait: If True, block until motion completes

methods.name: move_l
methods.doc:
Linear Cartesian move to target pose.

Returns the command index (≥ 0) on success, -1 on failure.

Category: Motion

Example:
    rbt.move_l([0, 263, 242, 90, 0, 90], speed=0.5)

Args:
    pose: Target [x,y,z,rx,ry,rz] in mm and degrees
    frame: Reference frame ("WRF" or "TRF")
    duration: Motion duration in seconds; > 0 times the move and speed is unused
    speed: Speed fraction in (0, 1], used when duration is 0
    accel: Acceleration fraction in (0, 1]
    r: Blend radius in mm
    rel: If True, pose is relative delta
    wait: If True, block until motion completes

methods.name: move_c
methods.doc:
Circular arc through current position -> via -> end.

Returns the command index (≥ 0) on success, -1 on failure.

Category: Motion

Example:
    rbt.move_c(via=[0, 250, 250, 90, 0, 90], end=[0, 263, 242, 90, 0, 90], speed=0.5)

Args:
    via: Via-point pose [x,y,z,rx,ry,rz]
    end: End-point pose [x,y,z,rx,ry,rz]
    frame: Reference frame
    duration: Motion duration in seconds; > 0 times the move and speed is unused
    speed: Speed fraction in (0, 1], used when duration is 0
    accel: Acceleration fraction in (0, 1]
    r: Blend radius in mm
    wait: If True, block until motion completes

methods.name: move_s
methods.doc:
Cubic spline through waypoints.

Returns the command index (≥ 0) on success, -1 on failure.

Category: Motion

Example:
    rbt.move_s([[0, 263, 242, 90, 0, 90], [50, 250, 200, 90, 0, 90]], speed=0.5)

Args:
    waypoints: List of poses [[x,y,z,rx,ry,rz], ...]
    frame: Reference frame
    duration: Motion duration in seconds; > 0 times the move and speed is unused
    speed: Speed fraction in (0, 1], used when duration is 0
    accel: Acceleration fraction in (0, 1]
    wait: If True, block until motion completes

methods.name: move_p
methods.doc:
Process move — constant TCP speed with auto-blending at corners.

Returns the command index (≥ 0) on success, -1 on failure.

Category: Motion

Example:
    rbt.move_p([[0, 263, 242, 90, 0, 90], [50, 250, 200, 90, 0, 90]], speed=0.5)

Args:
    waypoints: List of poses [[x,y,z,rx,ry,rz], ...]
    frame: Reference frame
    duration: Motion duration in seconds; > 0 times the move and speed is unused
    speed: Speed fraction in (0, 1], used when duration is 0
    accel: Acceleration fraction in (0, 1]
    wait: If True, block until motion completes

methods.name: servo_j
methods.doc:
Streaming joint position target. Fire-and-forget.

The stream stops about 0.25 s after the last target arrives: the arm
brakes to rest and holds there.

Category: Streaming

Example:
    rbt.servo_j([90, -90, 180, 0, 0, 180])

Args:
    angles: 6 joint angles in degrees (ignored if pose= is set)
    pose: If set, Cartesian target — dispatches to SERVOJ_POSE
    speed: Speed fraction 0-1
    accel: Acceleration fraction 0-1

methods.name: servo_l
methods.doc:
Streaming linear Cartesian position target. Fire-and-forget.

The stream stops about 0.25 s after the last target arrives: the tool
brakes along its line to rest and holds there.

Category: Streaming

Example:
    rbt.servo_l([0, 263, 242, 90, 0, 90])

Args:
    pose: Target [x,y,z,rx,ry,rz] in mm and degrees
    speed: Speed fraction 0-1
    accel: Acceleration fraction 0-1

methods.name: jog_j
methods.doc:
Joint velocity jog. Single-joint or multi-joint.

Single joint:   jog_j(0, 0.5, 1.0)
Multi joint:    jog_j(joints=[0,1], speeds=[0.5, -0.3], duration=1.0)

Category: Jog

Example:
    rbt.jog_j(0, speed=0.5, duration=1.0)

Args:
    joint: Joint index (0-5) for single-joint jog
    speed: Signed speed fraction for single-joint jog
    duration: Jog duration in seconds
    joints: List of joint indices for multi-joint jog
    speeds: List of signed speed fractions for multi-joint jog
    accel: Acceleration fraction 0-1

methods.name: jog_l
methods.doc:
Cartesian velocity jog. Single-axis or multi-axis.

Single axis:  jog_l("WRF", "X", 0.5, 1.0)
Multi axis:   jog_l("WRF", axes=["X","Y"], speeds_list=[0.5, -0.3], duration=1.0)

Category: Jog

Example:
    rbt.jog_l("WRF", "X", speed=0.5, duration=1.0)

Args:
    frame: Reference frame ("WRF" or "TRF")
    axis: Axis name for single-axis jog
    speed: Signed speed fraction for single-axis jog
    duration: Jog duration in seconds
    axes: List of axis names for multi-axis jog
    speeds_list: List of signed speed fractions for multi-axis jog
    accel: Acceleration fraction 0-1

methods.name: checkpoint
methods.doc:
Insert a checkpoint marker in the motion queue.

Returns the command index (≥ 0) on success, -1 on failure.

Category: Synchronization

Example:
    rbt.checkpoint("pick_done")

Args:
    label: Checkpoint label for progress tracking

methods.name: wait_checkpoint
methods.doc:
Wait until a checkpoint with the given label has been reached.

Category: Synchronization

Example:
    rbt.wait_checkpoint("pick_done")

Args:
    label: Checkpoint label to wait for
    timeout: Maximum wait time in seconds

methods.name: write_io
methods.doc:
Set digital output by logical index (0 = first output pin).

The firmware I/O byte layout is ``[in0, in1, out0, out1, estop, ...]``
so logical output index 0 maps to bit position 2.

Returns the command index (≥ 0) on success, -1 on failure.

``timeout`` bounds command acceptance. TimeoutError leaves application
unconfirmed; None uses the client defaults.

Category: I/O

Example:
    rbt.write_io(0, 1)   # Set first output HIGH

methods.name: delay
methods.doc:
Insert a non-blocking delay in the motion queue.

Returns the command index (≥ 0) on success, -1 on failure.

Category: Synchronization

Example:
    rbt.delay(1.0)

methods.name: tool_action
methods.doc:
Send a generic tool action command.

Returns the command index (>= 0) on success, -1 on failure. The
action and its parameters are checked before anything is sent: a
malformed one raises ``ValueError``. A key naming a tool other than
the selected one is refused by the controller.

A tool action is queued work: it runs in queue order with motion,
the arm holding still while it does, so a wait on it covers the
motion queued ahead of it, and one sent after a blended move ends
the blend there. A ``move`` before a completed ``calibrate`` is
refused when its turn comes, failing its own index; a tool action
that fails cancels what is queued behind it (``MOTN_CANCELLED``).
A pause holds the tool actions still queued. ``stop()``,
``estop()``, ``reset_state()``, a teleport, or a jog or servo stream
taking the arm discards them and halts the one running where the
jaws are, keeping the grip.

``stop`` alone acts at once, on the tool fitted now: it halts the
action running, failing it as cancelled by a tool stop, keeps what
is queued behind it, and holds the next queued tool action until
the jaws are still.

Electric grippers take ``move [position, speed, current]``
(exactly three fractions in ``[0, 1]``; current spans the tool's
``current_range``), ``calibrate``, ``stop`` (halt in place, keep
grip) and ``idle`` (release, the jaws left where they are);
``set_position``/``open``/``close`` map onto ``move``. Pneumatic
grippers take ``open``, ``close``, and ``move``/``set_position
[position]``.

Category: I/O

Example:
    rbt.tool_action("PNEUMATIC", "open")

Args:
    tool_key: Tool registry key (e.g. "PNEUMATIC", "SSG-48", "MSG")
    action: Action name (e.g. "open", "close", "move", "calibrate")
    params: Positional parameters (meaning defined by tool config)
    wait: If True, block until action completes
    timeout: Maximum time to wait in seconds (only used when wait=True)

methods.name: stream_status
methods.doc:
Async generator that yields status updates from multicast broadcasts.

Usage:
    async for status in client.stream_status():
        print(f"Angles: {status.angles}")

This generator terminates automatically when :meth:`close` is
called on the client, so callers do not need to manually cancel
their consumer tasks.

Each yielded StatusBuffer is a copy - safe to store or process async.
For zero-copy hot paths, use :meth:`stream_status_shared` instead.

Slow consumers automatically skip to the latest state (desired for real-time).

methods.name: stream_status_shared
methods.doc:
Zero-copy async generator that yields the shared status buffer.

Usage:
    async for status in client.stream_status_shared():
        # Process immediately - don't store references
        print(f"Angles: {status.angles}")

WARNING: The same buffer instance is yielded on every iteration.
Do not store references to the yielded object - data will be
overwritten on the next iteration. For safe storage, use
:meth:`stream_status` or call status.copy().

This generator terminates automatically when :meth:`close` is
called on the client.

Slow consumers automatically skip to the latest state (desired for real-time).

electric.name: stop
electric.doc:
Halt the jaws where they are, keeping the grip, ahead of anything
still queued: the action running fails as cancelled, and the queue
behind it is kept. On an uncalibrated gripper, which has no position
to hold, this releases instead.

electric.name: release
electric.doc:
Drop the grip, freeing the jaws for manual handling, once the
commands queued ahead of it have run. The jaws stay where they
are.

registered_tools.description: SSG-48 adaptive electric gripper (Spectral micro BLDC)

errors.name: IK_TARGET_UNREACHABLE
errors.title: IK: target unreachable
errors.cause: Target pose has no valid IK solution. {detail}
errors.remedy: Verify target is within workspace. Try different orientation.

errors.name: IK_PARTIAL_PATH
errors.title: IK: partial path failure
errors.cause: Only {valid}/{total} poses along the path are reachable.
errors.remedy: Shorten the move, add intermediate waypoints, or adjust orientation.

errors.name: TRAJ_EMPTY_RESULT
errors.title: Trajectory: empty result
errors.cause: Trajectory generation returned no waypoints. {detail}
errors.remedy: Check motion parameters. Start and end may be too close.

errors.name: TRAJ_NO_STEPS
errors.title: Trajectory: no steps
errors.cause: Trajectory calculation produced zero steps. {detail}
errors.remedy: Increase duration or reduce speed fraction.

errors.name: MOTN_HOME_TIMEOUT
errors.title: Homing timeout
errors.cause: Robot did not start homing sequence within timeout.
errors.remedy: Check serial connection and robot power. Ensure E-stop is released.

errors.name: MOTN_GRIPPER_TIMEOUT
errors.title: Gripper timeout
errors.cause: Gripper command timed out in state {state}.
errors.remedy: Check gripper connection and calibration.

errors.name: MOTN_GRIPPER_UNKNOWN
errors.title: Gripper: unknown state
errors.cause: Gripper entered an unknown internal state.
errors.remedy: Reset the controller and recalibrate the gripper.

errors.name: MOTN_SETUP_FAILED
errors.title: Command setup failed
errors.cause: Command could not be initialized. {detail}
errors.remedy: Check command parameters and robot state.

errors.name: MOTN_TICK_FAILED
errors.title: Command execution error
errors.cause: Unexpected error during execution. {detail}
errors.remedy: Check robot state. May need to re-home.

errors.name: MOTN_CANCELLED
errors.title: Command cancelled
errors.cause: The command was cancelled by {scope} before it finished.
errors.effect: The motion did not run to completion.
errors.remedy: Re-issue the command if the motion is still wanted.

errors.name: COMM_QUEUE_FULL
errors.title: Command queue full
errors.cause: Motion queue at maximum capacity.
errors.remedy: Wait for current motions to complete.

errors.name: COMM_UNKNOWN_COMMAND
errors.title: Unknown command
errors.cause: No handler for received command type.
errors.remedy: Check client library version matches server.

errors.name: COMM_DECODE_ERROR
errors.title: Command decode error
errors.cause: Failed to decode command. {detail}
errors.remedy: Check command encoding. Possible version mismatch.

errors.name: COMM_VALIDATION_ERROR
errors.title: Command validation error
errors.cause: Invalid parameters. {detail}
errors.remedy: Check parameter ranges and types.

errors.name: SYS_STATUS_RATE_INVALID
errors.title: Status rate not achievable
errors.cause: Status is broadcast every Nth control tick, so {requested} Hz does not divide the {control} Hz control loop evenly.
errors.remedy: Pick a rate that divides {control} Hz: {allowed}.

errors.name: SYS_CONTROLLER_DISABLED
errors.title: Controller disabled
errors.cause: Motion command sent while controller is disabled. {detail}
errors.remedy: Call reset() to re-enable the controller.

errors.name: SYS_ESTOP_ACTIVE
errors.title: E-stop active
errors.cause: Emergency stop is currently engaged.
errors.remedy: Release the E-stop button and call reset().

errors.name: SYS_PORT_SAVE_FAILED
errors.title: Serial port save failed
errors.cause: Could not save serial port configuration.
errors.effect: Port may not persist across restarts.
errors.remedy: Check file permissions and disk space.

errors.name: SYS_PROFILE_INVALID
errors.title: Invalid motion profile
errors.cause: Unrecognized motion profile: {detail}
errors.remedy: Use one of: TOPPRA, RUCKIG, QUINTIC, TRAPEZOID, LINEAR.

errors.name: SYS_NOT_SIMULATOR
errors.title: Simulator-only command
errors.cause: {detail} is only available on the simulator.
errors.effect: Command rejected; the arm is unchanged.
errors.remedy: Switch to the simulator with simulator(True), or drive the arm with a planned move.

errors.name: SYS_SELF_COLLISION
errors.title: Self-collision predicted
errors.cause: Planned configuration would self-collide at sample {sample} of {total}: {pairs}
errors.remedy: Choose a different target, add intermediate waypoints, or disable via PAROL6_COLLISION_CHECK=0.
